# Complete local World frame observations

`frame.tsv` records actual original `World.time`, `World.genesis`, and one preparation call to `Organism.die(null)`.
Every time call runs the complete ordinary local source frame.
No corridor is present.
Two source runs and the bundled JAR produced identical bytes.
All five compiled helper classes match across backends.

The fixed scope contains 27 cases, 71 snapshots, 233 actor views, and 45 dynamically discovered members.
There are 39 time calls, four genesis calls, and one preparation death.
Thirty-six discoveries come from actual genesis calls; nine come from synchronous reproduction or transformation.
Each actor view includes all 154 organism observation fields.

## Comparison contract

The fixed ledger, typed inputs, and exclusions precede Rust replay.
Compare nongeometric floating bits, gases, statistics, RNG, integers, ARGB, reactions, endpoints, bounds, identities, and ordering exactly.
Only organism `_m`, `_m1`, `_m2`, `_mass`, and `_I` retain the established geometry allowance.
For finite geometry, use `1e-10 * max(1, abs(expected))`.
Classify geometric NaN and signed infinity explicitly.
No velocity, energy, population, lifecycle flag, clock, or stored tree envelope receives an additional allowance.

Organism exclusions are `_world` and `_visibleWorld`.
World exclusions are `_visibleWorld`, `inCorridors`, `outCorridors`, and `_corridorexists`.
Selection is callback-routing metadata.
Y rows declare genotype reachability; all recorded scopes are observable.
Every other observation is a comparison obligation.
UI sidecars remain outside core parity and its row ledger.

## Real UI bootstrap

The helper checks four explicit private profile roots before accessing Preferences or simulation classes.
It requires `BGR_ISOLATED_XVFB=1` and an isolated display number of at least three digits.
The native driver creates each display through the existing `xvfb-run` route.
It never uses the user's desktop display.

Private preferences set initial population zero, English, software drawing, and disabled networking and backups.
The helper invokes actual `MainWindow.main` on the Swing EDT.
It requires a real paused MainWindow with no server thread.
It cancels the actual timer before scenario execution.
The real MainWindow, VisibleWorld, and InfoToolbar remain the collaborators for every source frame.
Each case attaches its real new World to that window.
No substitute UI class or intercepted callback supplies a result.

All setup, operations, and observations run on the EDT.
The helper does not enable the automatic simulation timer.
Original frame-zero and twenty-frame InfoToolbar callbacks execute normally.
Actual selection uses `VisibleWorld.setSelectedOrganism`.
`ui.tsv` records the actual selected identity and InfoToolbar energy, age, and mass text after each snapshot.
`bootstrap.json` records actual collaborator class names and the isolated display.
The three backends produce identical sidecar bytes in the recorded run.
Those sidecars demonstrate the reference bootstrap and callbacks, without claiming product UI or presentation parity.

Cleanup cancels every remaining MainWindow timer and disposes all windows on the EDT.
Secondary cleanup failures remain attached to the original error.
The helper always exits with its actual success or failure status.
The existing process runner then cleans its owned Java/Xvfb process group.

## Constructor and operation authority

Each case resets source defaults and records all 147 mutable primitive Utils settings.
Networking, automatic backup, and hardware acceleration remain disabled.
Ordinary explicit cases use zero initial attempts, oxygen setting `1000`, mutation bounds `0..10000`, and meta rate zero.
GREEN weight is seven; other weights are zero.
The seed is `827364` unless an explicit RNG input says otherwise.
Natural cohort cases retain the source's default genetic settings and all default color weights.

Initial g0, g1, g2, and g3 are explicit recipes.
g4 is an actual deep clone of g0.
Ordinary codes use one GREEN gene; g3 uses WHITE.
Lengths begin at twelve, symmetry one, mirror zero, mutation rate zero, generation 41, and clade `root`.
Targeted recipes supply their recorded colors, lengths, or additional genes before construction.
All recipe fields appear in input G/N blocks.
No observed child or expected snapshot becomes a constructor input.

A real new World starts with zero gases and empty membership.
Its constructor statistics still read the recorded initial settings.
Empty and cohort cases retain that exact initial distinction before genesis.
Ordinary actor cases explicitly set source gases through I before their real paste/add operations.
There is no hidden gas or statistics repair.

Cases contain zero, one, two, or three actual A actors.
Roles identify victim, killer, and optional selector.
Their ordinary centers are `(3500,3500)`, `(5000,5000)`, and `(1000,1000)`.
Controlled contact cases explicitly supply cached endpoints, integer/fractional centers, bounds, lengths, masses, inertia, and velocities.
Those inputs describe the test state; they do not claim a natural geometry rebuild.
Every later input precedes its actual operation.

K rows use the existing five-column structure.
`time,victim,~` means one actual World.time, including cases without a victim actor.
`genesis,victim,~` means one actual World.genesis using U settings and the current real RNG.
`die,selector,~` means actual selector.die(null), followed by the ordinary frame removal path.
The World-operation target is a protocol placeholder rather than a fabricated actor.
There are no B rows or substitute frame operations.

## Membership, identity, and frozen envelopes

D rows discover actual World members by object identity and membership order.
The `newbornN` counter resets per case and continues across genesis calls.
Numeric IDs can restart while D identities remain distinct.
The observer retains every known A/D object for O/H/Q after removal or genesis.
V `_organisms` records actual current membership, including removals and replacements.
It is an observed output, not a setup instruction.

Y roots include supplied recipes, all retained known actors, current members, and statistics holders.
A removed actor's code remains observable through the retained object and, where applicable, the frozen tree.
There are no rejected candidate or private-code exclusions.
The separate genetics corpus remains responsible for mutable per-Gene alias topology.

After time, J rows observe actual stored JTS envelopes.
The helper reads the pinned tree's existing pending ItemBoundables or packed root children.
It does not call build, insert, remove, replace, or reconstruct the tree.
It verifies that the pending list, root identity, and built flag remain unchanged during that observation.
J order uses the real pre-call membership order.
Each envelope comes from the actual stored entry, rather than a current actor rectangle or expected snapshot.
These bounded scenarios retain exact i32 envelope components.

Genesis emits no J rows and leaves the existing source tree unchanged.
A repeated-genesis case retains old tree objects while current membership contains new objects with reused numeric IDs.
The next time call replaces that tree normally.
Q rows invoke actual source queries and preserve actual returned identities and order.
The public query may perform normal lazy packing; the frozen-envelope observer performs no packing itself.

## Distinct complete-frame scenarios

Empty cases preserve new-World versus genesis gases, frame 255 rollover, sequential atmospheric conversion, and statistics publication.
The following frame zero executes the real InfoToolbar refresh.
A default 32-attempt cohort performs actual random generation and three complete frames.
A separate two-attempt cohort executes genesis, time, genesis, and time with retained old identities.

Growth contact restores the original growth ratio after collision while retaining source rescaling and `hasGrown`.
A border collision still reaches GRAY contact before displacement rollback.
EYE sensing can affect the actor before a later physical candidate returns a collision.
A real selected corpse removes at index zero while later original members still move.
The actual source selection-clearing callback remains recorded in the UI sidecar.

PLAGUE and YELLOW contacts append children synchronously during their parents' frames.
New children retain age zero and remain outside that frame's frozen tree.
The next time call includes them.
CORAL transformation and recipient removal preserve old frozen peer references and the newly appended body.

Immunity cases retain independent ordered draws, partial payments, negative delay, Lavender wrapping, and countdown arithmetic.
Plant cases distinguish update, Jade extra work, healing, leaf/methane work, seasonal frame zero, and live LIME crowding.
Countdown one blocks reproduction for that frame; countdown zero reaches the actual caller.
One case observes a plant update replacing a supplied early threshold before scheduling.
A separate equality case disables extra photo/update changes and observes no fallthrough to ordinary reproduction.
An infected adult exercises Lavender inhibition before any birth.

Mobile version-one spores remain inactive while their original random movement runs.
A separate version-five decay branch activates its organism, then the next frame executes active work.
Partial breathing can produce a retained corpse before later inactive maintenance.
A NaN-energy organism leaves membership through the strict move-return predicate without an invented additional death event.
All observations come from the real source methods.

## Isolation, preservation, and limits

Compile `tools/reference/FrameOracle.java` against each pinned backend.
Run `biogenesis.FrameOracle NEW_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY` with the exact isolated native arguments in provenance.
Positive runs have a 120-second bound; compilation uses sixty seconds; negative guards use thirty seconds.
Six actual guards cover each omitted profile root, an escaped preferences symlink, and existing-output preservation.
The helper refuses existing outputs and uses `CREATE_NEW`.

Final raw receipts remain under `.workflow-local/frame-oracle-790bb5ye/`.
The native capture is `.workflow-local/frame-native-rea-v2.json`.
The first successful capture, its helper, and the later compile failure remain preserved separately.
Before Rust replay, the observer gained stored-envelope observations and three distinct source-outcome scenarios.
No Rust output or production mismatch drove those changes.

All 74 original hash/size/mode pins, 159 compiled reference classes, and prior TSV fixtures retain their recorded hashes.
The exact prior count appears in provenance.
The native tool verifies cleanup for its owned process group.
It does not prove full-host process absence or observe network traffic.

These artifacts establish complete ordinary local Java frame observations.
Rust frame parity requires a separate strict replay and review.
Corridor arrival, outbound transfer, travelling presentation, full UI journeys, hardware behavior, and performance acceptance remain separate requirements.
They remain required compatibility work.
